text: We evaluated confidence regularization on the student's predictions (regularization weight 0.25) in a weak-to-strong setup where a pythia-410m weak supervisor teaches a llama-3.1-8b strong student, across 4 seeds. The weak supervisor reaches 0.56 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling accuracy is 0.73, while the transfer-trained student reaches 0.62 accuracy with a standard error of 0.02. This corresponds to a performance gap recovered (PGR) of 0.36 with a standard error of 0.14, compared with a baseline PGR of 0.21. Because the difference between the measured PGR and the baseline falls within two standard errors of the PGR estimate, the data do not establish that confidence regularization improves on the baseline; the point estimate is higher, but the uncertainty is large relative to that separation. With only 4 seeds, the variance estimate itself is weakly constrained. Further seeds, and ideally matched baseline standard errors, would be needed to determine whether the apparent ordering holds.
